# Resources

## Resources for R

### Books and Comprehensive Guides

- R for Data Science [@wickham2023r4ds] - comprehensive introduction to doing data science with R
- R Packages [@wickham2023rpkgs] - complete guide to R package development
- [Awesome R Package Development Tools](https://github.com/IndrajeetPatil/awesome-r-pkgtools) - curated list of tools for R package development
- Advanced R [@wickham2019advr] - deep dive into R programming and internals
- Mastering Shiny [@wickham2021shiny] - comprehensive guide to building web applications with Shiny
- Engineering Production-Grade Shiny Apps [@fay2021engineering] - best practices for production Shiny applications
- Happy Git and GitHub for the useR [@bryan2023happygit] - guide to using Git and GitHub with R
- [litedown: R Markdown Reimagined](https://pkg.yihui.org/litedown/book/) - a book by Yihui Xie on [`{litedown}`](https://pkg.yihui.org/litedown/), a lightweight R Markdown implementation aimed at simplicity and speed
- [DataCamp](https://www.datacamp.com/) - email Kristen for access

### UC Davis DataLab Workshops and Tutorials

The [UC Davis DataLab](https://github.com/ucdavisdatalab) provides extensive workshops and learning materials for data science:

- [Workshop Index](https://ucdavisdatalab.github.io/workshop_index/) - comprehensive catalog of all DataLab workshops
- [R Basics Workshop](https://github.com/ucdavisdatalab/workshop_r_basics) - foundational R programming for beginners
- [Research Toolkits](https://github.com/ucdavisdatalab/research-toolkits) - in-depth guides for research tools and methods
- [Install Guides](https://ucdavisdatalab.github.io/install_guides/) - setup instructions for data science software

### Cheat Sheets

- [Data transformation with dplyr cheat sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/data-transformation.html)
- [Data tidying with tidyr cheat sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/tidyr.html)
- [Data visualization with ggplot2 cheat sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/data-visualization.html)
- [data table cheat sheet](https://s3.amazonaws.com/assets.datacamp.com/blog_assets/datatable_Cheat_Sheet_R.pdf)
- [R Markdown cheat sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/rmarkdown.html)

### Style and Best Practices

- [Hadley Wickham's R Style Guide](http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Style.html)

### Data Documentation and Dictionaries

- [Tidyverse data-dict](https://data-dict.tidyverse.org/) - open specification and CLI tool for creating, validating, and documenting data dictionaries in YAML format

### Tidy Evaluation Resources

- [Tidy Eval in 5 Minutes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nERXS3ssntw) (video)
- [Tidy Evaluation](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/programming.html) (e-book)
- [Data Frame Columns as Arguments to Dplyr Functions](https://www.brodrigues.co/blog/2016-07-18-data-frame-columns-as-arguments-to-dplyr-functions/) (blog)
- [Standard Evaluation for *_join](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/28125816/r-standard-evaluation-for-join-dplyr) (stackoverflow)
- [Programming with dplyr](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/articles/programming.html) (package vignette)

## Resources for Git & Github

- Happy Git and GitHub for the useR [@bryan2023happygit] - comprehensive guide to using Git and GitHub with R
- [GitHub Learn](https://learn.github.com/) - official interactive courses,
  Skills exercises, learning pathways, and credentials
- [GitHub Skills: Introduction to GitHub](https://github.com/skills/introduction-to-github)
- [UC Davis DataLab Git Sandbox](https://github.com/ucdavisdatalab/sandbox_git) - hands-on Git practice repository
- [Claude Code on the Web: Auto-Fix Pull Requests](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web#auto-fix-pull-requests) -
  documentation on Claude Code's web interface for automatically investigating and resolving check failures and review comments on pull requests
- [Claude Code Workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows) -
  documentation on Claude Code's dynamic subagent orchestration feature for parallel codebase audits, migrations, and evaluations

## Practical Computing and Command Line

- [The Missing CS Quarter at UC Davis](https://missing.cs.ucdavis.edu/) - practical computing skills,
  shell tools,
  command-line workflows,
  and version control
  ([GitLab repository](https://gitlab.com/missing-cs-quarter-ucd/))

## Resources for Python

- [UC Davis DataLab Python Basics Workshop](https://github.com/ucdavisdatalab/workshop_python_basics) - foundational Python programming
- [Natural Language Processing with Python](https://github.com/ucdavisdatalab/workshop_nlp_with_python) - text analysis and NLP techniques

## Resources for Julia

- [UC Davis Julia Users Group Julia Basics Workshop](https://ucjug.github.io/workshop_julia_basics/) - foundational Julia programming

## Artificial Intelligence & Coding Agents

- [Working with AI (wai)](https://morrison-lab.github.io/wai/) - our lab's comprehensive guide
  to AI coding agents, harnesses, policies, and workflows
- [`pi`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) - minimalist, extensible AI agent toolkit
  providing a unified LLM API, interactive TUI, and terminal coding agent CLI

## Scientific figures

- Ten Simple Rules for Better Figures [@rougier2014]
- [Tufte CSS](https://edwardtufte.github.io/tufte-css/) - style HTML articles like Edward Tufte's books and handouts,
  with sidenotes, typography, and tight integration of graphics with text

## Writing

- Unpacking the Scientific Toolbox [@silbiger2019]
- ICMJE Definition of authorship [@icmje]
- Computational science: ...why scientific programming does not compute [@merali2010]
- [The Pathway to Publishing: A Guide to Quantitative Writing in the Health Sciences ](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-98175-4)
- [Principles of Scientific Writing](https://github.com/d-morrison/psw) - a handbook covering scientific writing principles including citations and evidence, word choice, and conciseness
- [Secret, actionable writing tips](https://x.com/acagamic/status/1680381737816424450)
